items.label: Console Mode
items.info:
Whether melonDS should emulate a Nintendo DS or a Nintendo DSi. DSi mode has some limits:

- Native BIOS/firmware/NAND files must be provided, including for the regular DS.
- Some features (such as savestates) are not available in DSi mode.
- Direct boot mode cannot be used for DSiWare.

See the DSi-specific options in this category for more information. If unsure, set to DS mode unless playing a DSi game. Changes take effect at the next restart.

items.label: Slot-2 Device
items.info:
The peripheral that will be inserted into the emulated console's Slot-2. Ignored in DSi mode, or if a GBA ROM is explicitly loaded. If a GBA ROM for any game in the Boktai trilogy is inserted, the corresponding Solar Sensor setting will be forced. In supported NDS games, each Boktai cart will have different effects. 
Changes take effect at next core start.

items.label: Use Host Light Sensor
items.info:
If enabled, the emulated solar sensor's light input will come from your device's real luminance sensor if available. If disabled or no sensor is available, the emulated sensor can be manually controlled with the following button combos:

- L+A+Up or L+A+Down
- Select+Up or Select+Down
- Your mouse wheel

Ignored unless "Slot-2 Device" is set to Solar Sensor, or if a ROM for any game in the Boktai trilogy (any region) is inserted in the emulated console's Slot-2. If unsure, leave enabled.

items.label: BIOS/Firmware Mode (DS Mode)
items.info:
Determines whether melonDS uses native BIOS/firmware dumps or its own built-in replacements. Only applies to DS mode, as DSi mode always requires native BIOS and firmware dumps.

Native mode uses BIOS and firmware files from a real DS. Place your dumps of these in the system directory or its "melonDS DS" subdirectory and name them as follows:

- DS BIOS: bios7.bin, bios9.bin
- DSi BIOS: dsi_bios7.bin, dsi_bios9.bin
- Firmware: See the "DS Firmware" and "DSi Firmware" options.
- DSi NAND: See the "DSi NAND " option.

Falls back to Built-In if any BIOS/firmware file isn't found.

Built-In mode uses melonDS's built-in BIOS and firmware, and is suitable for most games.

Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: DS Firmware
items.info:
Select a firmware image to use for DS mode. Files are listed here if they:

- Are inside the frontend's system directory, or a subdirectory named "melonDS DS".
- Are exactly 131,072 bytes (128KB), 262,144 bytes (256KB), or 524,288 bytes (512KB) long.
- Contain valid header data for DS firmware.

Nintendo WFC IDs are saved to firmware, so switching firmware images may result in the loss of some WFC data. Ignored in DSi mode or if BIOS/Firmware Mode is Built-In. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: DSi Firmware
items.info:
Select a firmware image to use for DSi mode. Files are listed here if they:

- Are inside the frontend's system directory, or a subdirectory named "melonDS DS".
- Are exactly 131,072 bytes (128KB), 262,144 bytes (256KB), or 524,288 bytes (512KB) long.
- Contain valid header data for DSi firmware.

Nintendo WFC IDs are saved to firmware, so switching firmware images may result in the loss of some WFC data. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: DSi NAND Path
items.info:
Select a DSi NAND image to use. Required when using DSi mode. Files are listed here if they:

- Are inside the frontend's system directory, or a subdirectory named "melonDS DS".
- Are exactly 251,658,304 bytes (240MB) or 257,425,472 bytes (245.5MB) long with valid footer data, OR;
- Are 64 bytes shorter than these lengths and contain equivalent data at file offset 0xFF800.

Set to "Auto" to let the core pick a NAND image whose region matches the loaded DSiWare ROM. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Boot Mode
items.info:
Determines how melonDS boots games.

Native: Load games through the system menu, similar to the real DS/DSi boot process. Requires native BIOS and firmware files in the system directory.
Direct: Skip the system menu and go straight to the game. Supported for DSiWare if native DSi system files are available.

Ignored if loaded without a game (Native is forced) or if using Built-In BIOS/Firmware (Direct is forced). Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Virtual SD Card (DSi)
items.info: If enabled, a virtual SD card will be made available to the emulated DSi. The card image must be within the frontend's system directory and be named dsi_sd_card.bin. If no image exists, a 4GB virtual SD card will be created. Ignored in DS mode. Changes take effect at next boot.

items.label: Read-Only Mode (DSi)
items.info: If enabled, the emulated DSi sees the virtual SD card as read-only. Changes take effect with next restart.

items.label: Sync SD Card to Host (DSi)
items.info: If enabled, the virtual SD card's files will be synced to this core's save directory. Enable this if you want to add files to the virtual SD card from outside the core. Syncing happens when loading and unloading a game, so external changes won't have any effect while the core is running. Takes effect at the next boot. Adjusting this setting may overwrite existing save data.

items.label: Virtual SD Card
items.info: If enabled, a virtual SD card will be made available to homebrew DS games. The card image must be within the frontend's system directory and be named dldi_sd_card.bin. If no image exists, a 4GB virtual SD card will be created. Ignored for retail games. Changes take effect at next boot.

items.label: Read-Only Mode
items.info: If enabled, homebrew applications will see the virtual SD card as read-only. Changes take effect with next restart.

items.label: Sync SD Card to Host
items.info: If enabled, the virtual SD card's files will be synced to this core's save directory. Enable this if you want to add files to the virtual SD card from outside the core. Syncing happens when loading and unloading a game, so external changes won't have any effect while the core is running. Takes effect at the next boot. Adjusting this setting may overwrite existing save data.

items.label: Battery Update Interval
items.info: How often the emulated console's battery should be updated. Ignored if the frontend can't get the device's battery level.

items.label: DS Low Battery Threshold
items.info: If the host's battery level falls below this percentage, the emulated DS will report that its battery level is low. Ignored if running in DSi mode, no battery is available, or the frontend can't query the power status.

items.label: Time Mode
items.info:
The initial time of the emulated console's internal clock.

- Real: Start in sync with your device's clock.
- Synchronized: Synchronize the emulated clock to your device's clock. May cause unexpected behavior in some games when rewinding or fast-forwarding.
- Relative: Start in sync with your device's clock, plus or minus a specified offset. Will be constrained to dates that the DS can represent.
- Absolute: Start at a specific date and time, regardless of your device's clock.

All dates and times are in your local timezone. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Time Offset (Years)
items.info: The number of years to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Time Offset (Days)
items.info: The number of days to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Time Offset (Hours)
items.info: The number of hours to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Time Offset (Minutes)
items.info: The number of minutes to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Year
items.info: The initial year to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Month
items.info: The initial month to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Day
items.info: The initial day of the month to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Days that extend past the end of a month will roll over to the next (e.g. April 31st will become May 1st). Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Hour
items.info: The initial hour to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Starting Minute
items.info: The initial minute to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Render Mode
items.info:
Software mode is faster and more accurate, while OpenGL mode supports scaling up the resolution of 3D graphics in most cases.

OpenGL mode may be buggy on some graphics hardware. If it doesn't work, software rendering is used as a fallback. Changes take effect immediately but may require the frontend's video driver to be restarted.

items.label: Internal Resolution
items.info: The degree to which the emulated 3D engine's graphics are scaled up. Dimensions are given per screen. OpenGL renderer only.

items.label: Improved Polygon Splitting
items.info: Enable this if your game's 3D models are not rendering correctly. OpenGL renderer only.

items.label: Threaded Software Renderer
items.info: If enabled, the software renderer will run on a separate thread. Changes take effect immediately. If unsure, leave this enabled.

sections.label: Audio
sections.info: Settings for audio output and microphone input.

items.label: Microphone Input Mode
items.info:
Choose the sound that the emulated microphone will receive:

Silence: No audio input.
Blow: Loop a built-in blowing sound.
Noise: Random white noise.
Microphone: Use your real microphone if available, fall back to Silence if not.

items.label: Microphone Button Mode
items.info:
Set the behavior of the Microphone button, even if Microphone Input Mode is set to Blow or Noise. The emulated microphone receives silence when disabled by the button.

Hold: Button enables mic input while held.
Toggle: Button enables mic input when pressed, disables it when pressed again.
Always: Button is ignored, mic input is always enabled.

Ignored if Microphone Input Mode is set to Silence.

items.label: Audio Bit Depth
items.info: The number of bits used for each audio sample. Automatic matches the original hardware's behavior by using 10-bit audio for DS mode and 16-bit audio for DSi mode. If unsure, set to Automatic.

items.label: Audio Interpolation
items.info: Interpolates audio output for improved quality. Disable this to match the behavior of the original DS hardware.

items.label: Cursor Mode
items.info: Determines when a cursor should appear on the bottom screen. Never is recommended for touch screens; the other settings are best suited for mouse or joystick input.

items.label: Cursor Timeout
items.info: If Cursor Mode is set to "Until Timeout", then the cursor will be hidden if it hasn't been moved for a certain time.

items.label: Touch Mode
items.info:
Determines how the console's touch screen is emulated.

Joystick: Use a joystick to control the cursor. Recommended if you don't have a mouse or a real touch screen available.
Pointer: Use your mouse or touch screen to control the cursor.
Auto: Use either Joystick or Pointer, depending on which you last touched.

If unsure, set to Auto.

items.label: Joystick Cursor Deadzone
items.info: If the joystick is within this deadzone the cursor will not move.

items.label: Joystick Cursor Max Speed
items.info: Set the max speed for the joystick cursor.

items.label: Joystick Cursor Response
items.info:
Set the response curve for the joystick cursor.
Linear is a response curve where the cursor speed is 1:1 with the joystick input.
Quadratic is a response curve that reduces the sensitivity near the joystick center for finer control, but increases the sensitivity near the edges

items.label: Joystick Cursor Multiplier
items.info: Set the multiplier for the joystick cursor when the speedup/slowdown pointer button (L2 by default) is held

items.label: # of Screen Layouts
items.info: The number of screen layouts to cycle through with the Next Layout button.

items.label: Hybrid/Largescreen Ratio
items.info: The size of the larger screen relative to the smaller ones when using a hybrid or largescreen layout.

items.label: Hybrid Small Screen Mode
items.info: Choose which screens will be shown when using a hybrid layout.

items.label: Hybrid/Largescreen Filtering
items.info:
Affects how the hybrid/largescreen screen is scaled up.

Nearest: No filtering. Graphics look blocky.
Linear: Smooth scaling.

items.label: Screen Gap
items.info: Choose how large the gap between the screens should be. Vertical layouts (including rotations) only. Dimensions exclude the effects of the frontend's scaling.

items.label: Secondary Screen Scale
items.info: The size of the secondary screen relative to the primary screen. Applies to vertical layouts (Top/Bottom, Bottom/Top). At 100%, both screens are the same size. At 50%, the secondary screen is half the width and height of the primary screen.

items.label: Secondary Screen Filtering
items.info:
Affects how the secondary screen is scaled down.

Nearest: No filtering. Graphics look blocky.
Linear: Smooth scaling. Recommended when using Secondary Screen Scale below 100%.

items.label: DNS Override
items.info:
The DNS server to use for the emulated access point ("melonAP"). Use this to play online with custom servers that reimplement the discontinued Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection services. Game support depends on the server. 
Some internet service providers may block requests to these servers. If this is the case for you, see https://tinyurl.com/393cb755 for a workaround.

The listed servers are not affiliated with libretro, Nintendo, the melonDS team, or this core's author. Please respect other players and follow the server's rules.

If unsure, leave on Kaeru WFC. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Language
items.info:
Overrides the language mode of the emulated console.

Use Host: Uses the frontend's language if supported by the console.
Don't Override: Use whatever language is already set on the firmware. This is the fallback behavior if the emulated DS (or DSi NAND) doesn't support the frontend's language.

Not every game honors this setting. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Username
items.info:
Overrides the username given to the emulated console.

Don't Override: Uses whatever name is defined on the firmware.
Guess: Try to get your username from the frontend. If that fails, try the USER, USERNAME, and LOGNAME environment variables.
melonDS DS: Uses "melonDS DS". This is the default if nothing else works.

Names are truncated to 10 characters. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Favorite Color
items.info: The theme ("favorite color") of the emulated console. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Birth Month
items.info: The month of your birthday. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Birth Day
items.info: The day within the month of your birthday. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Enable Alarm
items.info: Whether the emulated console's alarm is enabled. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Alarm Hour
items.info: The hour of the configured alarm. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Alarm Minute
items.info: The minute of the configured alarm. Changes take effect at next restart.

items.label: Network MAC Address Mode
items.info:
Configures how the emulated console's MAC address is set. Changing this option might make local multiplayer impossible or block access to save files in games that use the MAC address to prevent tampering of save files (i.e. Pokémon).
No relation to the direct mode interface. Changes take effect at next restart.
See https://bit.ly/4fJtWKN for more information.

items.label: Networking Mode
items.info:
Configures how melonDS DS emulates Nintendo WFC. If unsure, use Indirect mode.

Indirect: Use libslirp to emulate the DS's network stack. Simple and needs no setup.
Direct: Routes emulated Wi-Fi packets to the host's network interface. Faster and more reliable, but requires an ethernet connection and that libpcap is installed. If unavailable, falls back to Indirect mode.

Changes take effect at next restart. Not related to local multiplayer.

items.label: Network Interface (Direct Mode)
items.info: Select a network interface to use with Direct Mode. If unsure, set to Automatic. Changes take effect at next core restart.

items.label: JIT Recompiler
items.info: Recompiles emulated machine code into native code as it runs, considerably improving performance over plain interpretation. Takes effect at next restart. If unsure, leave enabled.

items.label: Fast Memory
items.info: Takes effect at next restart. If unsure, leave enabled.

sections.label: On-Screen Display & Notifications
sections.info: Change what extra information is shown on-screen.

items.label: Warn About Unsupported Features
items.info: Enable to display an on-screen message if melonDS tries to use certain unsupported features. These warnings will be logged regardless of this setting.

items.label: Warn About Certain BIOS Problems
items.info: Enable to display warnings if your BIOS files have certain known problems. A warning will always be shown if your BIOS files are missing or invalid, regardless of this setting.

items.label: Show Screen Layout
items.info: Enable to show which screen layout within the configured sequence is active.

items.label: Show Host Microphone State
items.info: Enable to show whether your device's microphone is active.

items.label: Show Host Camera State
items.info: Enable to show whether your device's camera is active.

items.label: Show Lid State
items.info: Enable to show whether the emulated screens are closed.

items.label: Show Sensor Reading
items.info: Enable to show the emulated input of any peripheral sensors that aren't already managed by one of the other OSD options, e.g. the solar sensor embedded in the Boktai trilogy's carts. If no peripherals (including GBA carts) are available, this option will have no effect.
